invariants: all stateful transport operations are inherent instance methods
Server owns exactly one listener
Server.localEndpoint observes the operating-system-selected IPv4 or IPv6 endpoint without transferring or cloning the listener
Connection owns exactly one accepted transport
readRequest consumes one Connection state and returns one Request owner while preserving reusable transport state
Request owns transport bytes and parsed spans together
Request.localEndpoint and Request.remoteEndpoint observe the retained accepted transport without ambient server state
request bytes grow in one bounded caller-owned buffer
receiveAppend writes only unused capacity and does not copy the prefix
openBody consumes Request into one affine RequestBody and rejects a second body read
the exact positive receive-buffer capacity is explicit and invalid sizes fail before transport I/O
the parsed head continues to borrow only the stable original request buffer
initial over-read bytes are decoded in place through BodyDecoder.writeRange
later transport reads reuse a separate RequestBody-owned buffer through receiveInto
readInto returns after existing progress or at most one transport receive to preserve caller backpressure
readInto recognizes an already complete empty body before transport receive
RequestBody.finish validates decoder completion once and returns one Request owner
all suffix bytes already read past body completion remain owned by the returned Request
a complete pipelined request head is parsed in place through Parser.parseRequestBytesRange without copying its bytes
an incomplete retained suffix is compacted exactly once into one maxHeadBytes-bounded owner before later receives
an empty reusable receive buffer is refilled in place through receiveInto without allocating a new request buffer
request body decoding introduces no intermediate encoded-input or decoded-body copy
respond consumes Request and ResponseHead
response body storage remains caller owned and is sent without an intermediate body copy
persistent response requires completed request-body framing before any response bytes are sent
at most one retained buffer may contain response-time leftover bytes
close mode closes the transport and returns ResponseOutcome.Closed
persistent mode returns ResponseOutcome.Reusable with exactly one affine Connection and every retained suffix byte
Connection.close consumes and closes the retained transport
socket HTTP and ownership failures remain explicit Result values
unsupported: concurrent or out-of-order pipelined response scheduling
HTTP client pooling redirects and cookies
